h1: The 5 Best Wired Video Doorbells of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Wired Video Doorbells 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five wired video doorbells from WYZE, Ring, Blink and Reolink, sorted by resolution, power type and budget bucket.
summary: The WYZE Wired Doorbell Camera v2 is the best wired video doorbell: 2K, hardwired power and a $50 to $100 price. The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro is the only 4K model here. The Blink 2K+ is the cheapest, the Ring 2K Plus suits Ring loyalists, and the REOLINK is the pick if an Ethernet cable already reaches the door.
intro: "Wired" covers two quite different installs, and buying the wrong one wastes a weekend. Some doorbells tap the low-voltage transformer behind your existing chime. Others, like the PoE model here, draw power through an Ethernet cable run to the door. Resolution is the number everyone compares, but power method decides whether the camera works at all.

We reviewed five wired doorbells and ranked them on listed resolution, power method and price bucket. Facts for several models are thin, so where a listing leaves out chime, storage or subscription details we say so instead of guessing. Read the live listing for those terms before you buy, because recurring cloud fees change the real cost of a doorbell more than the sticker price does.

products.name: WYZE Wired Doorbell Camera v2
products.verdict: 2K wired video in the $50-100 bucket is hard to argue with.
products.description:
The WYZE Wired Doorbell Camera v2 is a hardwired 2K doorbell in the $50 to $100 bucket. Two things make it the baseline most buyers want: video sharper than 1080p, which helps when you zoom on a face or a package label, and power from your wiring, which spares you battery charging and the dead-battery gaps that plague wireless doorbells.

It ranks first because it matches the Ring 2K Plus on resolution while costing less. The Blink 2K+ is cheaper still, but WYZE has the more established listing. The tradeoff against the Ring 4K Pro is plain: you give up 4K detail to stay in a lower price bucket.

Buy it if you already have doorbell wiring and want strong value. The caveat is that our listing facts cover resolution and power only, so verify chime and storage options yourself. Skip it if you want 4K or have no wiring at the door.
products.idealFor: Households with existing doorbell wiring who want solid video for less.
products.skipIf: You want 4K detail or have no wiring at the door.

products.name: Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro
products.verdict: The only 4K wired doorbell in this ranking.
products.description:
The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro is a hardwired doorbell with 4K video, priced in the $100 to $200 bucket. Resolution is its headline spec and nothing else here matches it. More pixels matter for a doorbell because the view is wide and the subject, a face or a license plate across the street, may occupy a small slice of the frame.

It lands below the WYZE because you pay at least a bucket more for the extra detail, and many porch views are already sharp at 2K. Against the Ring 2K Plus, it is the clear step up for similar money, which makes it the better Ring if you buy the brand.

Buy it if image detail is the point and the budget allows. The caveat is Wi-Fi: 4K only helps if the signal at your door can carry it. Skip it if 2K is enough and you want to stay under $100.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want maximum video detail at the front door.
products.skipIf: 2K is enough and you want to spend under $100.

products.name: Blink Wired Doorbell 2K+
products.verdict: The cheapest 2K wired doorbell in the group.
products.description:
The Blink Wired Doorbell 2K+ offers 2K video on wired power in the $25 to $50 bucket, the lowest price tier in this ranking. Hardwired operation means no battery swaps, and the 2K label puts it level with the WYZE and the Ring 2K Plus on resolution. It is the cheapest way here into a wired video doorbell.

It sits third because the WYZE gives you the same resolution with a more established spec listing, while the Blink wins purely on cost. Against the Ring 2K Plus, it saves a couple of price buckets for the same listed sharpness. The question is whether the missing detail matters to you.

Buy it if price is the deciding factor. The caveat is thin documentation: we have no listed detail beyond resolution and power, so check chime, storage and subscription terms before ordering. Skip it if you want the most complete listing.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who still want 2K video and wired power.
products.skipIf: You want the most detailed listing before buying.

products.name: Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus
products.verdict: Ring's 2K wired option, at a $100-200 price.
products.description:
The Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus is a 2K hardwired doorbell in the $100 to $200 bucket. It pairs Ring's app and camera lineup with transformer power, so a household already running Ring cameras can manage everything in one place.

It ranks fourth because the WYZE and Blink deliver the same resolution for less, while the Ring 4K Pro offers a real step up for a similar price. That leaves the 2K Plus in an awkward middle, the pick for people set on the Ring brand but not on 4K. You pay a premium for the ecosystem and the name, not for sharper video.

Buy it if you want to stay inside the Ring ecosystem and do not need 4K. The caveat is the price premium over equally sharp rivals, so skip it if you shop on value alone.
products.idealFor: Ring loyalists who do not need 4K.
products.skipIf: You are shopping on value alone.

products.name: REOLINK Video Doorbell PoE 2K Wired Outdoor Security Camera
products.verdict: The pick if you have an Ethernet cable at the door.
products.description:
The REOLINK Video Doorbell PoE is a 2K doorbell powered over Ethernet, in the $100 to $200 bucket. One cable carries both power and data, so there is no transformer behind the chime and no dependence on Wi-Fi strength at the door. That combination makes it steady in homes where wireless signal fades near the entry.

It ranks last only because PoE needs a network run that many homes lack, unlike the transformer-powered picks above. If you do have that cable, it removes the need for doorbell wiring entirely, and the signal does not depend on Wi-Fi at the door. Without the cable, installation gets complicated fast.

Buy it if a network cable already reaches your door or you are building a wired camera system. The caveat is the Ethernet requirement, and it costs more than the WYZE. Skip it if you only have a standard doorbell transformer.
products.idealFor: Homes with a network cable already at the entry.
products.skipIf: You only have a standard doorbell transformer.

whatMatters.detail: Resolution is the pixel count of the video, written as 2K or 4K on the listing. It matters because a doorbell sees faces and packages from a short distance, and more pixels hold up better when you zoom in. Look for the number in the title or bullets, and remember that Wi-Fi quality limits what you actually get, and a weak signal turns 4K into a stuttering picture.

Wired models either tap your doorbell transformer or use Power over Ethernet through one network cable. This matters because the wrong match means rewiring or a failed install. Check what already runs to your door, then confirm the listing's power wording says wired or PoE. Voltage and chime type matter too, so read the install notes.

Doorbell prices range from the $25 to $50 bucket up to $100 to $200 in this ranking. It matters because identical 2K video exists across several buckets, so a higher price is not automatic proof of better video. Compare resolution first, then decide what the extra money buys. A bucket jump should bring a feature you will use.

Ring, Blink and WYZE each run their own app and camera lineup. It matters because mixing brands means more than one app to open, and separate subscriptions. Check whether you already own cameras from one of them, and lean that way if so, especially when you want one view for all cameras. Check app support on your phone too.

Some listings spell out chime, storage and subscription terms and others say little. It matters because hidden recurring costs change the real price. Scroll to the product description and read what is and is not included before ordering, and treat missing detail as a question for the seller, and compare any monthly fee against the sticker price.

faq.q: Do wired doorbells need an existing doorbell?
faq.a: Most transformer-powered models reuse your existing doorbell wiring. PoE models like the REOLINK need an Ethernet cable instead. Check which one you have before buying, because a WYZE v2 or Blink will not run on a network cable, and PoE needs a switch or injector.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Buying on resolution alone and ignoring how the unit is powered. A 4K Ring Pro is great with transformer wiring, and a REOLINK PoE doorbell is useless without a network cable at the door.

faq.q: Is the Ring 4K Pro worth it over a 2K model?
faq.a: Only if you want extra detail from the video. The WYZE and Blink deliver 2K for less, and for most porch views that is already sharp. Choose the 4K Pro for long driveways or tight crops, where zooming into a small frame matters.

Wired setup involves connecting to existing wires or a network cable, so it takes more effort than a battery model. Follow each listing's included guidance, and cut power at the breaker before touching a Ring or WYZE transformer.

Wired power removes battery charging. Occasional cleaning of the lens and checking connections is all we would expect. Wipe the camera window with a soft cloth and tighten the terminals once a year if the picture ever flickers.

faq.q: Is the eufy E340 on this list?
faq.a: No. Its listing says battery-powered, so it does not match a wired-only title. Every pick here, from the WYZE v2 to the REOLINK PoE, takes continuous power from a wire or cable, so none depends on battery swaps.

finalTake: Buy the WYZE v2 if you want sharp 2K video from existing doorbell wiring at a modest price. Move to the Ring 4K Pro only if detail at the door justifies the premium, and the Blink 2K+ when budget leads. Choose the REOLINK PoE model if a network cable already reaches your entry. Match the power method to your wiring before you compare pixels.
